anf_compare.notes: ANF has no text of this homily; translated directly from the PG 93 Greek.

bible_refs.note: ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ resumes the verse quoted just before (Καὶ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ); cited inline in Pass B beside the clause.

choices.english: his word held some hidden meaning
choices.why: τὸν λόγον is Christ's saying 'I will make you fishers of men' (u02-open); τι is kept as 'some'.

rejected: they came to be above the earth
choices.why: The perfect states the change in their standing; 'rose' gives it in natural English without adding a claim.
διάκονος here is service, not the church office.

choices.term: οὐχ ὡς ὑπὸ τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀλλ' ὑπὲρ τῶν
choices.english: not, as it were, beneath the heavens, but above the…
rejected: not under heaven but beyond it
choices.why: ὡς is kept as 'as it were'; the row breaks at ὑπὲρ τῶν, and οὐρανῶν opens u02-rem-mid.

pass_a_gloss: [continuing from u02-open: '…but heeding the one who called and made firm by faith and'] having perceived the word to hold something hidden, they followed him; and immediately they have come to be above the earth, and they were seen more glorious than kings, like to angels, ministers of God, heralds of salvation, servants of immortality, more brilliant than sun and moon and stars; for of these men the glory [is] not as under the heavens but above the [heavens, which continues in u02-rem-mid].
pass_b_english: …perceiving that his word held some hidden meaning, they followed him (Matthew 4:20). At once they rose above the earth and were seen to be more glorious than kings: like angels, ministers of God, heralds of salvation, servants of immortality, more radiant than sun, moon, and stars. For their glory is not, as it were, beneath the heavens, but above the…
source_text:
τὸν λόγον ἔχειν τι νενοηκότες ἀπόκρυφον, ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ· καὶ παραχρῆμα τῆς
γῆς ἄνω γεγόνασι καὶ βασιλέων ὤφθησαν ἐνδοξότεροι, ἀγγέλων ὅμοιοι, λειτουργοὶ
θεοῦ, σωτηρίας κήρυκες, ἀθανασίας διάκονοι, ἡλίου καὶ σελήνης καὶ ἀστέρων
ἐκλαμπρότεροι· τούτων γὰρ ἡ δόξα οὐχ ὡς ὑπὸ τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀλλ' ὑπὲρ τῶν
notes: The row begins mid-sentence: the subject and the first participles (τῷ καλοῦντι προσέχοντες καὶ τῇ πίστει βεβαιωθέντες καὶ) close u02-open, whose English ends '…made firm by faith, and…'; the opening ellipsis marks the join, so the conjunction is not repeated.
τούτων refers to the apostles, whose glory is set above the heavenly lights just named. Daniel 12:3 or Matthew 13:43 may be echoed, but the wording is not close enough to cite inline.

review.coverage: every clause checked against the source
changes: removed a repeated opening 'and' that already ends u02-open
'something hidden' -> 'some hidden meaning' to keep τι
'like the angels' -> 'like angels' (no article in the Greek)

reviewer: claude source review, separate pass (same model family as the drafter)
